summary: The copy is dry, instrumental and matches DUMMIES' voice: no barks, no cheer, and the hit-stop is not redeclared. The problems are data and presentation rules. Two thresholds have no parameter ID, several shock rings and rays exceed the burst size cap, the rings use reserved cue roles, one sound is nearly identical to the spent-car thud, and the head-on layer describes zone damage that P1 no longer uses.

issues.rule: Every value needs a registry parameter ID. 400 is a bare threshold with no ID, and it is half of damage.bodyHealth only by coincidence.
issues.fix: "proto.hits.impact.big.assessedMin" (add a param: value 400, unit "assessed impact", purpose "Assessed impact at which the big-hit layer applies.", sources ["ENG#8.2~1"])

issues.rule: Every value needs a registry parameter ID. The tight-pass gap of 0.5 m is a bare number with no ID.
issues.fix: "proto.hits.nearMiss.tightGap" (add a param: value 0.5, unit "m", purpose "Closest gap at which a near miss counts as a very tight pass.", sources ["DESIGN#D4.5"])

issues.rule: The impact burst cue is capped at 2 × body width (52 units). The registry purpose for ringRadiusMax already says to stay under that.
The impact burst cue is capped at 2 × body width (52 units). The head-on rays exceed it.
The impact burst (ring and rays) is capped at 2 × body width (52 units). A big-hit ring of 70 overruns the cap and can cover neighbouring cues (D4.5, J4).

issues.found: Heavier shake and double shock ring on the full-damage zone; crunch and horn
issues.rule: In the P1 damage model the zone factors are unused and angle replaces them, so the front zone is not a 'full-damage zone'. It is only the logged contact zone.
issues.fix: Heavier shake and a second, wider shock ring on a front contact; crunch and horn

issues.rule: Cue treatments are reserved. A decorative ring in cue.primary or cue.secondary reads as the battery glow ring or the commit ring. This applies to the rings in layers[0], [1], [5] and [8], whose roles are primary, secondary, primary and primary.

A scored hit and a physical touch on a spent car must not use indistinguishable feedback. The stopped-car scored thud (400→90 Hz, 0.14 s) is nearly the same as the spent-touch thud (420→110 Hz, 0.14 s).
issues.fix: Give the stopped scored hit a different sound, for example a lower, longer thud with the crunch. Set thudFrom to 300, thudTo to 60 and thudSeconds to 0.22, so the dull spent-touch thud is not repeated.

issues.rule: The stumble amplitude is an angle (the purpose says radians). Its unit must match its value.
